anomalies.observed: In the Capacitive Touch Button (TSC) block, the two hierarchical labels NET0012 and NET0013 are drawn on the same node feeding R6, which then goes to the BTN pin of the TSC electrode A3. C16 (22n) is also tied to this same node and to GND.
anomalies.expected: The TSC electrode (BTN) should be driven from one MCU TSC IO through the 1k series resistor, while the sampling capacitor (22n) should be on a separate TSC IO of the same group, not shorted to the electrode net.

evidence.quote: NET0013 / NET0012 labels both connect to R6 (1k) which drives A3 pin 1 (BTN); C16 22n connects to the same node and GND.
TSC_G2_IO2: U2 pin 57 (PB5) — R8 (1 kΩ series resistor) — A2 pin "BTN" (the touch electrode); TSC_G2_IO4: U2 pin 59 (PB7) — C14 (22 nF to GND) — this is the TSC sampling capacitor for the group

anomalies.impact: If NET0012 and NET0013 are truly shorted, the electrode and sampling-capacitor IOs are bridged, so the TSC peripheral cannot perform charge-transfer sensing correctly and the touch button will not work.

parsed.summary: The schematic appears largely consistent with the specification, but the capacitive-touch block shows the two TSC nets (NET0012 and NET0013) apparently tied together at the series resistor/sampling capacitor node, which would prevent the STM32 TSC peripheral from sensing the electrode correctly.
